fair_value.method: Approved driver build (FY28 revenue 9,334, non-GAAP op margin 33.6%) at the horizon: NTM ex-SBC EPS ~$16.06 x 19.8x (= 21.7x SBC-costed; peer median 21.45x shrunk from own 23.24x, less 1.15 turns of post-horizon risk) = ~$318 (w 0.7), plus a mid-cycle check $11.55 x 23x = $265.65 (w 0.3): research target (12m) $302.26.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-11-02 ~$16.06 (ex-SBC, incl. interest on ~$1.75B net cash; 171.5M shares) x 19.8x

inputs_detail.value: 19.8x on ex-SBC NTM EPS at 2027-11-02 (= 21.7x SBC-costed)
inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median 21.45x (VIAV 18.8, FTV 20.5, TER 22.4, AME 26.0). Own 303.5 / 13.06 Zacks FY27 (SBC expensed) = 23.24x. Exit 21.45 x (23.24/21.45)^0.8 = 22.87x; less 1.15 turns of post-horizon risk = 21.72x on SBC-costed EPS; the engine's P/E reads NOPAT before SBC, so x (1 - 8.8%) (SBC 3% of revenue x 0.86 / NTM EPS ~16.06 = $1.42 = 8.8%) = 19.8x.
inputs_detail.variant_view: No post-horizon deduction (exit 22.87x SBC-costed = 20.86x engine) adds ~$17 to the leg, ~$12 to the target (4%, under the card threshold).

inputs_detail.derivation: Approved driver set (Kilian 2026-11-02), used unchanged: Wireline quarterly estimates (flag: not disclosed): FY25 229/257/290/310 (=1,086; share of CC rising 40->47%, wireline grew double digits FY25 per Q4 FY25 remarks), FY26 358/428/520 (Q3 > wireless 486) and Q4 585 (FY26 1,891). FY growth = 1/3 x market growth (manufacturing test scales with units) + 2/3 x R&D growth (estimate +25% FY27, +15% FY28, +10% FY29; no source, the main judgment): FY27 +42.0% -> 2,685, FY28 +20.2% -> 3,228, FY29 +15.7% -> 3,734. downside.story: 10th percentile: a China shock (China revenue -50% = ~8.7% of FY27 revenue: entity listings or retaliation cut wireless, EI and semis test in China; ADG barely exposed) lands on top of an AI-optics digestion in which double-ordered transceiver capacity is absorbed (LightCounting: a correction is more likely than a soft landing; transceiver sales turn ~6 months before capex), so wireline capture of the optics market falls 30% below base as test buying of 1.6T lines pauses; margins fall back toward FY24-25 (CSG -4.5pt, EISG -4pt) as the tariff refund and synergy tailwinds are gone and volume leverage reverses; the market pays ~14.8x ex-SBC EPS (~13.5x SBC-costed, below VIAV's 18.8x) for falling EPS; normalised EPS 15% lower.

base.story: Approved drivers deliver (FY27 revenue 8,425, +18%; FY28 9,334) but the market prices KEYS near the test-and-measurement peer median, not as an AI winner, because margins are at a cycle peak, supply governs conversion and the optics market's own analysts expect a correction: research target (12m) roughly flat to today.

upside.story: 90th percentile: supply eases by mid-2027 and the $2B+/quarter order book converts; 1.6T and 3.2T R&D test plus manufacturing test scale with a market still growing ~30%+ in 2028, wireline capture 25% above base; operating leverage adds 1.5-2pt of margin; the market pays ~24.3x ex-SBC (~22x SBC-costed, near AME) because the FY29 path still grows.

thesis_break_reason: $215 (-29%, ~13.4x the build's NTM ex-SBC EPS, below every whole-company peer): at that level the market would be pricing an order collapse (book-to-bill well below 1 after the 1.13 of Q3 FY26), a China entity-list event, or margins back at FY24's ~25%, i.e. the optics-driven earnings path itself is broken, not ordinary 45%-vol noise. It sits above my P10 because the P10 is that break happening.

Hyperscaler Q4 calls: CY2027 capex guides (LightCounting: 2027 outlook not clear until ~January)

key_uncertainties: Whether the $2B+/quarter orders include shortage-driven double ordering that reverses (LightCounting July 2026).

China (17.5% of FY25 revenue): US entity listings of optics/telecom customers or Chinese retaliation naming Keysight.
AI-optics market path after 2027: Big-4 capex growth slowing from ~70% to ~30% in 2027 (LightCounting assumption).

reverse_dcf_check: 19.8x ex-SBC (21.7x SBC-costed) NTM P/E at the horizon on ~$16.06 EPS implies, at ~9-10% cost of equity, ~8-10% EPS growth for five years after FY2029 with ~33% margins held; plausible only if AI-optics test spend keeps growing through a 2028 digestion, which is why the multiple carries 1.15 turns off and a 30% weight sits on mid-cycle earnings.

sbc_treatment.note: FY25 SBC $162M (F29), TTM $214M (F32). Costed in FCF via sbc_treatment 'cost'; the engine's P/E reads ex-SBC NOPAT, so the P/E multiple is scaled x 0.912 (SBC = 8.8% of NTM EPS) to put it on an SBC-costed basis; the normalised leg's stated EPS is after SBC. Share count falls only by buybacks net of SBC issuance (-0.7%/yr).

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Credit is not where the risk is: net cash (-88 at Q3 FY26), BBB/positive at S&P, $700M current notes coverable from $2.6B cash; insider activity is director selling only (30k shares at $286 in March, 3k at $319 in August, $4.1M sold and $0 bought over 3 months to April), short interest only 1.3% of float, no short report found. The bear case is cyclical: KEYS earns its highest margins ever (33-34% non-GAAP op margin vs ~25% in FY24-25; FY24 revenue fell 9%) on an AI-optics ramp whose own industry analyst (LightCounting, July 2026) calls a correction more likely than a soft landing and warns of double ordering in record backlogs; the CFO says supply will be the governor and FY26 profit includes a one-time IEEPA refund; the stock fell from $389.93 to $303.50, sold off after both of the last two beats. I keep the approved drivers unchanged (they sit ~3-5% above Street revenue FY27-28: 8,425 vs 8,195, 9,334 vs 8,927) and put my skepticism in the valuation: a P/E at the shrunk peer median less 1.15 turns for post-horizon risks, plus a 30% weight on mid-cycle earnings at a 29% margin. Research target (12m) ~ flat to today vs the Street's $418 average. The downside case (P10 ~$174) combines the mandated China shock (-50% China revenue) with an optics digestion and margin mean reversion; upside (P90) is supply easing and 1.6T/3.2T scaling. Research was limited: no transcript full text (Benzinga/Chartmill blocked), no non-USD peer consensus.

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by the approved quarterly driver set (wl_capture x LightCounting optics market, wireless_rev, adg_rev, ei_rev, csg_margin, eisg_margin; unchanged) valued with a peer-anchored NTM P/E at the horizon on the build's own EPS (19.8x ex-SBC = 21.7x SBC-costed, weight 0.7) and a normalised mid-cycle P/E cross-check (stated EPS $11.55 at a 29% mid-cycle margin x 23x, weight 0.3; not driver-linked). No DCF (policy), no SOTP (CSG and EISG have no separable listed peer multiples). The method-fit flag (thin XBRL TTM revenue tags) does not weaken the P/E legs: revenue and segment income come from the Ex.99.1 releases; the normalised leg is the non-multiple-on-consensus check.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) driver disagreement (not in the set): wl_capture FY28 ~8% lower (3.56% vs 3.87%) on LightCounting's correction view would cut the target ~$7; csg_margin 34-34.5% is a peak, my mid-cycle is ~29% (carried in the normalised leg, not the drivers). (2) 1.15 turns off the exit rule for post-horizon risks moves the target ~-4% (under the 5% card threshold). (3) SBC: the engine's P/E reads ex-SBC NOPAT while Zacks peers are mixed; I cost SBC by scaling the multiple x 0.912. (4) China shock probability: I size a China revenue -50% event at ~12% within 3 years (entity-listing of large Chinese optics/telecom customers or retaliation naming Keysight; the June 2026 MOFCOM list did not name it, A&P) and carry it in the downside case and a 0.35-turn post-horizon deduction. Financing: none probable (net cash, BBB positive; the $700M current notes refinance or repay from cash; p of an equity raise <5%).
model_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 19.8x ex-SBC (21.7x SBC-costed) NTM P/E at the horizon on ~$16.06 EPS implies, at ~9-10% cost of equity, ~8-10% EPS growth for five years after FY2029 with ~33% margins held; plausible only if AI-optics test spend keeps growing through a 2028 digestion, which is why the multiple carries 1.15 turns off and a 30% weight sits on mid-cycle earnings.
